Owner, 2026-09-30 (L37, L38): 'leave place for animations, images, 3D illustrations - graphic things in slides - and mention what kind would be used', and 'make these tests more variable - not only choose A B C D - as much variable as possible ... more digitalized, more realistic, more detailed, more technical; if you cannot perform, explain why and advise how'. Read by scripts/content_script.py (Stage 3: every slide names its visual; every task names its mechanic; the variety floors are checked) and scripts/make_architecture_page.py (Stage 2: the visual plan per module and who makes it). mechanics._law: No free typing on a self-check or module check (owner C11, course-task-ux §2) - every mechanic below is answered by tapping, dragging or setting a control. The 'answer' format is the one line-per-item text the operator edits in the Word file; '*' marks what is right.

single_choice.answer: options A, B, C (D); 'correct' is one letter

multi_select.answer: options A, B, C, D (E); 'correct' lists the letters, e.g. A, C

choose_and_justify.en: Choose the action, then the reason
choose_and_justify.answer: options are the actions, 'correct' one letter; the answer box lists the reasons, one per line, the right one marked *

order.answer: one step per line, in the right order - the tablet shuffles them

match.answer: one pair per line: left = right

categorise.answer: one group per line: Group: item; item; item

cloze.en: Complete the sentence (choose the missing words)
cloze.answer: the sentence, each gap as [right* | wrong | wrong]

hotspot.en: Tap the right place on the picture
hotspot.answer: one tappable area per line, the right one(s) marked *; the picture is named in 'visual'

label_diagram.en: Drag the labels onto the drawing
label_diagram.answer: one label per line, each the name of a part the drawing shows

spot_the_hazard.en: Find the hazards in the scene
spot_the_hazard.answer: one area of the scene per line, the real hazards marked *

read_instrument.answer: what the display shows, then the options - the reading and what it means; 'correct' one letter

set_value.answer: one line: value unit ± tolerance, range low-high - e.g. -42 °C ± 2, range -60 to 20

panel_operate.en: Operate the panel or line up the valves
panel_operate.lv: Darbini paneli vai sagatavo vārstu līniju
panel_operate.answer: one control per line: control = the state it must end in; the panel or drawing is named in 'visual'

scenario.en: Scenario - decide, see what happens, decide again
scenario.lv: Scenārijs - izlem, redzi sekas, izlem atkal
scenario.ru: Сценарий - реши, увидь последствия, реши снова
scenario.answer: one step per line: the situation => right action* | wrong | wrong

trainee_tablet_experience._law: L42 (owner, 2026-10-01): 'tablet-friendly UI/UX, user-friendly, but max modern, max technology and max understandable - so people even with zero tablet experience do the tasks, and they are excited.' The full rule: course-task-ux SKILL.md section 0.
trainee_tablet_experience.first_time_gesture_hint: a short animated hand, once per kind of task
trainee_tablet_experience.result_screen: the trainee's own score as an animated ring - rewarding, professional, never childish
never: an error message to the trainee
a timer on a self-check or module check
proved_by: step 6: every task type at tablet size in a browser
QA: a 'never used a tablet' walkthrough in a colleague's browser
the owner's real-tablet touch test at the end (L39)

three_d._authority: Owner, 2026-10-07 (L46, 2.22.0): 'now he does 3D models almost every slide - cut it down to 50%, better not quantity but quality, use it only where it makes sense; and it lags a little in these 3D models, maybe optimisation can be considered - but mainly I love these 3D models.' Second message, same day: 'I also don't need you to cut the quality of 3D models - don't make it in all slides, about 50% of the presentation is the max that can be 3D models, but also don't cut quality, and put it only on slides where it makes sense, not only because you can.'
three_d._max_share: At most half of the presentation's teaching slides are 3D (model_3d, model_3d_scan, model_3d_licensed). Counted once a module has 2 slides with 3D or more - one 3D model in a short module is always fine. A must-fix in the content script and in the built deck (each .slide carries data-visual); the architecture page counts the plan. The cap is on how many - never on how good: every 3D model that stays is made at full quality.
three_d._in_a_row: A suggestion: more than 2 slides in a row with a 3D model - a photograph, a drawing or an animation between them gives the eye a rest.
fits: equipment and structures whose shape, inside or arrangement in space is what is taught - cargo tanks and containment systems, hull sections and spaces, pumps, compressors, valves, manifolds, piping runs, the reliquefaction plant, an enclosed space and its access
something the trainee must later recognise or operate on board, seen from every side
a cut-open view, where the inside is the lesson
does_not_fit: charts, curves, tables and matrices - a risk matrix, a vapour-pressure curve
symbols, signs, documents and binders - the SMS, a checklist, a permit
ideas and models of thinking - Swiss cheese, the steps of a risk assessment, the order of a procedure
a flat process that a flow or step animation shows better
decoration - 3D added only because it can be
three_d._flat_words: A 3D slide whose picture description uses one of these words gets a suggestion: a 3D model of something flat adds weight, not understanding.
three_d.quality: Each 3D model that stays gets the care of a main picture: true proportions, real materials (steel, insulation, paint), clear labels, a cut-open view where the inside is taught, and a starting view that already shows the point. Fewer, better.

performance._principle: Never a lesser look to make it faster (owner, 2026-10-07: 'don't cut quality'). The speed comes from how the scenes run - one renderer, built and freed with their slide, nothing drawn or recomputed while nothing changes - not from fewer details, blurrier pictures or plainer light.
performance.pixel_ratio: Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2) - sharp on the tablet's screen; 1 looks blurry there, an uncapped ratio of 3 costs more than the eye can see
rules: One WebGL renderer for the whole deck, shared by every 3D slide - never one per figure or per kit.

A scene is built when its slide comes up (or the slide before it), not when the deck opens; it is freed (geometry, materials, textures disposed) once the deck is two slides past it - at most two scenes alive.
Draw only while the slide is on screen and something moves or is being touched; when nothing changes, no frame is drawn. An automatic turn stops at the first touch.

Shadows keep their full, soft look - and are worked out once while the model is still (renderer.shadowMap.autoUpdate = false; shadowMap.needsUpdate = true only when something in the scene moves). Same picture, a fraction of the work.
The environment light (PMREM) is made once for the whole deck and shared, not once per scene.
Pixel ratio Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2); antialias on; preserveDrawingBuffer off (it changes nothing on screen).
Detail stays where the eye sees it; repeated parts (bolts, rungs, pipe supports) are one instanced mesh - the same look, drawn in one go.
Textures and .glb models compressed without visible loss (KTX2 / meshopt via gltf-transform), their decoders bundled in the module's assets; any file at most 15 MB (the classroom's limit).
Labels over the model move only when the view changes, not on every frame.
A still picture of the model (a poster) shows at once; the 3D takes over when it is ready - and the poster stays if the tablet has no WebGL.
performance.measured: In Chrome DevTools with the CPU slowed 4x (a stand-in for the classroom tablet): each 3D slide shows its first frame in under a second and turns at 30 frames a second or more - at full quality. The owner confirms on the real tablet at the end (L39).
performance.checked_by: check_course_package.py notes, from the module's own scripts: more than one renderer, shadows recomputed on every frame, preserveDrawingBuffer on, a pixel ratio of 1 (blurry) or uncapped

floors._every_slide: Owner, 2026-09-30 (2.18.1): no quota. As many pictures as the theory and the experience call for - wherever a picture, an animation or a realistic 3D illustration reflects what is being taught at that point, put it in; animation and 3D especially. A slide with none gets a suggestion, never a block. A picture that is named must say what it shows (must fix), and an unknown kind is a mistake to correct. 3D is the exception (owner, 2026-10-07, L46): at most half of a module's pictures, and only where it makes sense - see three_d.
floors._moving: A suggestion, not a rule (2.18.1): a module with this many minutes of theory and nothing that moves, turns or can be explored is pointed out, because where something moves, changes state or has an inside, a still picture teaches it worse (course-visuals, learning-needs.json).
floors._kinds: A suggestion, not a rule (2.18.1): a module of 6 slides or more with fewer than 3 kinds of picture is pointed out - but a picture is never added only for variety (L13).
floors._tasks: A self-check uses at least 2 different mechanics and a module check at least 3; 'choose one answer' is at most 40 % of a module's questions; every module has at least one hands-on question - locate, operate or decide on something that looks like the real thing; never more than 2 questions of the same mechanic in a row. These stay rules (owner, 2026-09-30). The final assessment follows the programme's own format - none of them applies to it.
